dct_description_sm: The purpose of the NCP Publications Database is to make the publications that have resulted from the Northern Contaminants Program (NCP) more accessible. The NCP works to reduce and, wherever possible, eliminate contaminants in traditionally harvested foods, while providing information that assists informed decision making by individuals and communities in their food use. The NCP is managed by Indian and Northern Affairs Canada, in partnership with other federal departments, the three territorial governments and northern aboriginal organizations. The NCP was established in 1991, and during its first five years was part of the federal government's Arctic Environmental Strategy (AES). The NCP works closely with the Arctic Council's Arctic Monitoring and Assessment Programme (AMAP), and the results of NCP projects represent the main Canadian contribution to AMAP. More details are available on the Northern Contaminants Program website.
